_comment: THE MCP METHOD LEDGER — what the protocol's own revisions say exists.
Read by scripts/spec_conformance.py. Governed by docs/LANDSCAPE_TRACKING_POLICY.md's
Rule 3 in spirit: a watch list nobody audits is a list of the things you already
thought of, so this file is REFRESHED FROM UPSTREAM rather than maintained by hand.
`spec_conformance.py --refresh` re-derives every set below from the specification
repository and refuses when this file disagrees with it.
THIS FILE DOES NOT DEFINE THE GATE'S POPULATION. The population is every
method-shaped string in our own shipped surface — the live query. This ledger is
only used to CLASSIFY those strings. Adding a revision here can move a string from
unclassified to classified; it can never add a string to the population. That is
assetlib_sweep.py's invariant, one instrument over, and it is the reason a gate over
a roster somebody curated is not the same thing as a gate.
A method is NEVER deleted from this file. When a revision removes one, the row stays
and gains a `removed_in` and a `migration` — so a later refresh cannot re-litigate a
question already answered, and so the gate can tell a reader what to write instead.
Fields:
revisions[]              every published revision, oldest first
revisions[].methods[]    the exact JSON-RPC method strings that revision defines
revisions[].source       the URL the set was derived from
extensions{}             methods that live in an extension rather than in core
migrations{}             removed method -> what to say instead, quoted from the spec
declared                 what WE negotiate, and where that value comes from

note: We do not set protocolVersion anywhere. `grep -rn protocolVersion host/src` is empty.
The negotiated value is min(what the client asks for, the SDK's LATEST), so an SDK
bump moves it without a line of ours changing. sdk-drift.yml already rebuilds weekly
against the newest in-range SDK, so this is foreseeable rather than hypothetical.

revisions.note: Identical method set to 2024-11-05 — that revision's changes were transport and auth, not method names.
The breaking one: thirteen methods removed, three added. `initialize` and `ping` have zero occurrences anywhere in this revision's schema, so their absence is a removal and not a naming artifact.

io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks.note: Only schema/draft/ exists upstream; there are no versioned directories yet. An extension method is NOT a core method — a description that names one is telling the reader about a surface the core spec no longer defines.

migrations.initialize: server/discover, or inline per-request `_meta` version negotiation. Spec: "Servers MUST implement `server/discover`. Clients MAY call it but are not required to."
migrations.notifications/initialized: no replacement — the handshake it belonged to was removed with `initialize`.
migrations.logging/setLevel: the capability field `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel`. Spec: "Replaces the former `logging/setLevel` RPC."
migrations.tasks/get: the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension, which keeps the name. Removed from CORE.
migrations.tasks/cancel: the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension, which keeps the name. Removed from CORE.
migrations.tasks/list: NO SUCCESSOR ANYWHERE — not in core, not in the extension.
migrations.tasks/result: NO SUCCESSOR ANYWHERE — poll `tasks/get` instead. Not in core, not in the extension.
